# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
instance

```
[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
```

which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.

## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here

Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.

For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
`Sigma.desc`.

The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
`ChartsCoverLocally` below.

## The honest scope, stated up front

`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
none to check.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity

/-!
# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
index per point of `T`".

**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
connection is what this file supplies.

## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:

* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
  strengthening chosen to be provable.
-/

    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]

    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (b : ℤ)

    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
    ∃ m' : ℕ, ∃ Z' : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor, t ∈ chartLocus C m' Z' lam :=
  ⟨m, Z, mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ b hb hdeg⟩
